subject: Renewal: EU onshore + APAC standby — data residency constraints
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@medquanta.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Choi <sara.choi@medquanta.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: EU onshore + APAC standby — data residency constraints

Hi Rafael,

Hope you’re well. Our renewal with Redwood is coming up (end of Sept) and we need to lock in two changes before we sign:

1) Primary EU residency: we need the service and logs for EU traffic to be on EU-hosted instances (for GDPR and our internal audit).
2) APAC standby/burst: ability to route APAC traffic to a standby cluster in APAC for capacity spikes, with cross-region failover in an outage.

We have a couple of constraints: no customer-level logs stored outside the EU except aggregated telemetry, and any failover must preserve data residency commitments (no permanent storage outside EU).

Can you share an updated SOW and rough pricing (committed vs. burst rates)? Also: timeline — we’re targeting a Q4 go-live for the EU node and want APAC standby in place by EOY. I’ve attached a short list of GDPR questions and a high-level dataflow diagram.

Tom
Tom Ellis
Head of Procurement, MedQuanta Ltd
Attachments: GDPR-DataFlow-questions.pdf

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@medquanta.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 12:04:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: EU onshore + APAC standby — data residency constraints

Hi Tom — thanks for the clear ask and the diagram.

Summary of what we recommend:
- EU primary node: Dedicated onshore node (EU-FR) handling EU traffic and storing PII/logs within EU.
- APAC standby: Standby cluster in APAC (SG) configured for burst capacity and as automated failover for availability. Failover will use in-region cache transfer; no persistent customer logs will be written outside EU unless the customer explicitly opts in.
- Contract changes: convert your monthly pay-as-you-go to a 12-month reserved capacity commit for the EU node (saves ~20% on committed baseline). APAC standby billed as reserved standby + usage-based burst for high volume.

I’ve attached an initial SOW draft and our SOC2 scoping checklist so you can share with legal/security. Key open items for procurement/legal: egress/telemetry language, audit evidence windows, and SLA credits for cross-region failover.

Proposed next steps:
1) We (Monica) will run through the SOW and open a narrow SOW amendment with explicit residency clauses.
2) Ben to confirm target throughput & GPU tier for EU node so we size the commit.
3) Rafael to get procurement pricing and DocuSign SOW ready.

Can we book a 30-min call on Tuesday to walk legal/security through the SOW?

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-eu-apac-draft-sow.pdf; redwood-soc2-scoping.docx

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 08:35:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: EU onshore + APAC standby — data residency constraints

Tom/Team — quick technical notes from SE side:

- Throughput: to keep latency <200ms for 512-token med-latency workloads we recommend a baseline of 4x A100-equivalent per EU cluster for your expected QPS (we can validate with logs).
- Caching: prefix/KV caching on EU node only; failover to APAC will use a best-effort KV sync for active sessions, but we will not persist raw message logs to APAC storage.
- Failover behavior: automatic failover is supported for availability but we’ll include an opt-in policy for customers that need cross-region persistent storage.
- Canary & staging: suggest a 2-week canary in EU with traffic split before full cutover.

I’ll upload a sizing worksheet after I pull your last 30 days of usage (Monica — can you share access?).

—Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@medquanta.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Sara Choi <sara.choi@medquanta.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 10:02:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Renewal: EU onshore + APAC standby — data residency constraints

Rafael / all —

Thanks for the fast responses and the SOW draft. A couple of items from legal:
- Please add a clause that aggregated telemetry may be transmitted out of-region but raw request/response and audit logs must remain in the EU region.
- We need a defined RTO for failover (we’re targeting <5 mins) and clear SLA credit language if cross-region failover causes any data residency breaches.

Also confirming timeline: Q4 EU go-live is still our objective; APAC standby by EOY is fine if we have a firm schedule. We will get procurement signoff once the SOW includes the residency/egress language and a final price.

I’m copying Sara (legal) who will coordinate the final redlines.

Tom

1) SOW amendment: Monica will produce an amendment this week with explicit residency/egress language and an RTO/RPO clause for failover. Draft will include the 5-minute failover target and SLA-credit formula.

Monica — please pick this up as the onboarding lead. Tom/Sara — I’ll set a 30-min walkthrough on Friday.
